newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt underpinned by nearby shortage.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt underpinned by nearby shortage.

text.p: A shortage of nearby material is helping to underpin cobalt despite claims by several consumers that prices were tending lower following the ending of the seven-month civil war in former Zaire.

Zaire's -- renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo after Lauren Kabila's forces toppled former president Mobutu Sese Seko -- state run mining company Gecamines was believed to be not moving any material from its dilapidated and cash starved facilities.
"There are no signs that cobalt from this region is finding its way into Europe," one source close to the producer said.
One trader suggested that a large European player in metals was air freighting cobalt from the Shaba province to avoid the transport disruptions, though this could not be confirmed.
Another said that production at Gecamines was running at extremely low levels and they were completely sold out prior to the fall of Mobutu.

Zambia, another producer of cobalt was also said to be experiencing production problems. Traders said the problems were causing a short-fall of around 5,000 tonnes of cobalt a year. North American producers were said to be running low stock levels.
Traders noted news that mining deals struck with the previous government will have to be renegotiated under the new administration.

The continued civil unrest in the capital, Kinshasa, since Kabila's victory was not seen likely to make much difference to an already unreliable cobalt supply situation from the country's mining region.
On Wednesday high grade cobalt was indicated at around $25.50 an ounce, against levels of $19 in the early part of 1997. Lower graded ingots was at around $22.50, versus $18.50.
